about: The share of construction spending that bears sales and use tax, by technology: JEDI's own taxable base, its "Sales Tax (Materials & Equipment Purchases)" line, at JEDI's default project. Where the workbook computes that tax, the share is the tax over (JEDI's rate times JEDI's cost before sales tax); where it does not, the materials and equipment share of JEDI's default cost. EIA's capital costs exclude sales tax (the report's words: "Equipment and material costs are intended to be the delivered costs inclusive of purchase price, duties, and freight, (but excluding any sales tax)"), so the tool adds the tax on this share of the reader's capital cost (docs/methods/forecast.md, section 5). Read from the saved workbooks (runs/w4/probe.csv requests 5 to 8) by chain 239, session 4201, 13 November 2026.
source: National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR, formerly NREL), JEDI models, https://www.nlr.gov/analysis/jedi/models

utility_pv.note: JEDI's PV model computes no sales tax at its defaults: DefaultData!D59, Sales Tax Exemption (percent of local taxes), is 1 (100 percent). The share here is the base the tax would fall on where a state taxes these purchases.

geothermal.note: JEDI's geothermal model has no sales tax line (searched for "sales tax" and "taxable" in every sheet): no taxable share is held, and the tool shows no sales tax figure for geothermal unless the reader types a share.
